issues.title: REPL expressions inside blocks
issues.result: Actual PTY sessions now display 0–9 from the original loop and 5 from the file-write block. The same CPython input agrees; displayhook and function-scope controls also pass.
issues.expected: The interactive REPL must display expression values in compound statements.
issues.limits: The new run is macOS/Rosetta, not Linux. Earlier Linux PTY evidence is reused separately. A new exclusive file path and os._exit prevent overwriting files or REPL history.
issues.related: [PR #7067](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7067): display interactive expressions in nested blocks

issues.title: Native OrderedDict export
issues.result: The native import succeeds, and ordering, move_to_end, popitem, reversed, equality and a subclass sample agree with CPython.
issues.expected: from _collections import OrderedDict must expose the native implementation.
issues.limits: This verifies the reported native export and exercised operations, not all OrderedDict behavior.
issues.related: [PR #8780](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8780): native OrderedDict and class-method descriptors

issues.title: ElementTree parsing valid XML
issues.result: The original empty root parses successfully. Valid child, text, attribute, namespace and UTF-8 samples agree with CPython.
issues.expected: `etree.XML("<root></root>")` must parse valid XML without the None-encoding TypeError.
issues.limits: A separate malformed input, ``, is still accepted where CPython raises ParseError. That difference prevents a full XML-compatibility claim but does not reproduce the original valid-XML TypeError.
issues.related: [PR #6582](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6582): accept None as the parser encoding; [PR #8741](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8741): native ElementTree parsing

issues.title: Disassembly support used by modulefinder
issues.result: The three requested dis APIs operate on actual bytecode. A five-module import graph and all 17 original ModuleFinderTest tests pass without skip or expectedFailure.
issues.expected: The requested dis exports and instruction iteration must support the reported modulefinder path.
issues.limits: Opcode numeric equality is not required. Creating a generator from integer 100 is not evidence of bytecode iteration; valid code bytes were iterated instead.
issues.related: [PR #5377](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5377): provide dis exports and bytecode/import scanning

issues.title: SymPy import with the reported versions
issues.result: SymPy 1.11.1 with mpmath 1.2.1 imports successfully. Tracing observes the original power.py:378 is_commutative assignment, and the reported Pow path succeeds.
issues.expected: The already installed reported package versions must import without the descriptor AttributeError.
issues.limits: The same dependency files were used in RustPython and CPython and their RECORD hashes were checked. Package installation and the full SymPy suite were not rerun.
issues.related: [PR #6390](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6390): install declared slot descriptors even over inherited attributes

issues.title: Finalization of a global object
issues.result: The unchanged original lifetime pattern prints deleted! at interpreter shutdown, with exit 0 and no stderr. An explicit-del control was checked separately.
issues.expected: The global object destructor must run during ordinary interpreter shutdown.
issues.limits: Process-abort paths and arbitrary shutdown ordering are not promised.
issues.related: [PR #6934](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6934): module finalization during shutdown

issues.title: Safe path flags and path insertion
issues.result: Script, -c, -m, symlink and actual PTY REPL checks confirm -P and PYTHONSAFEPATH suppress automatic unsafe paths; environment, -E and -I controls agree with CPython.
issues.expected: sys.flags.safe_path, -P and nonempty PYTHONSAFEPATH must control actual automatic sys.path insertion.
issues.limits: The four -m -E/-I fixture lookup failures are expected: those options remove the explicit module search environment. TERM=dumb caused a basic REPL fallback in both interpreters.
issues.related: [PR #4611](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/4611): connect -P, the environment and safe_path flags; [PR #5049](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5049): condition automatic path insertion on safe_path; [PR #8605](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8605): resolve script paths for path insertion

issues.title: Locale support for FormatSpec n
issues.result: Basic n and the original locale tests pass. Across five available locales, 395 formatting results include 102 differences: 84 zero-padding cases and 18 other Unicode-separator width cases.
issues.expected: Locale-sensitive n formatting must preserve grouping and character-based field width.
issues.limits: The zero-padding defect was rerun on native ARM64 too. The fr_FR U+202F width counterexample was run with Rosetta RustPython; >20n produces 18 characters rather than 20.
issues.related: [PR #7350](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7350): use locale grouping, separator and decimal-point data

issues.title: Native class-method descriptor type
issues.result: Both original descriptor queries return classmethod_descriptor. Binding and representative additional native descriptors agree with CPython.
issues.expected: Native class methods must use the classmethod_descriptor type.
issues.limits: No claim is made about every descriptor or every introspection API.
issues.related: [PR #8780](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8780): native OrderedDict and class-method descriptors

issues.title: Negative dynamic format width
issues.result: The original assertion preserves the two trailing spaces in `'abc  '`. Positive, zero and additional negative-width controls also agree with CPython.
issues.expected: A negative dynamic width selects left alignment.
issues.limits: The checked formatting cases do not establish every formatting combination.
issues.related: [PR #4766](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/4766): left alignment for negative dynamic widths

issues.title: Deque subclass pickle state
issues.result: The original regression test passes. Protocols 0–5 preserve dict/slots state, type, contents and maxlen in 36 subclass round trips.
issues.expected: Pickling a deque subclass must preserve its instance state.
issues.limits: The issue snippet accidentally pickles pickle.HIGHEST_PROTOCOL itself. That literal and the corrected intended input are separate. Recursive deque pickle is outside this reported nonrecursive case.
issues.related: [PR #7699](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7699): include __getstate__ in deque reduction

issues.title: README API documentation link
issues.result: The README destination returned HTTP 200 and an actual RustPython 0.6.0 API page, including crate and API content; status alone was not the oracle.
issues.expected: The README link must serve API documentation rather than an error or generic page.
issues.limits: This is the externally served page observed on October 5, 2026, not a documentation build from the baseline commit. CPython comparison does not apply.
issues.related: [Published API documentation](https://docs.rs/rustpython/latest/rustpython/)

issues.title: Surrogate in a type name
issues.result: The original surrogate is retained and type creation raises UnicodeEncodeError, matching CPython. Exit 1 for the uncaught exception is expected.
issues.expected: A surrogate-containing type name must raise UnicodeEncodeError instead of being silently replaced.
issues.limits: A separate adjacent-surrogate input is rejected by both, but UnicodeEncodeError.end differs (2 versus 3). Full error-span parity is not claimed.
issues.related: [PR #5629](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5629): retain surrogate literals; [PR #6547](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6547): validate type names as UTF-8

issues.title: Lambda in a class decorator
issues.result: The original source compiles without the Rust compiler panic. Executing that original source raises BaseFTests NameError in both interpreters. Separate valid mock.patch and nested-capture controls execute and restore the patched function.
issues.expected: Compilation must not panic when a class decorator contains a lambda argument.
issues.limits: The original application is not runnable as written; compile success is not application success. The normalized runtime examples are separate inputs.
issues.related: [PR #8138](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8138): visit class decorators before entering their class scope

issues.title: Await in an async comprehension
issues.result: The original async function compiles. The comment's actual asyncio event-loop and two awaited sleeps finish with lc done.
issues.expected: Await inside an async-function comprehension must not be rejected as outside an async function.
issues.limits: Calling the original await print(...) function correctly raises TypeError because print returns None. Compilation and execution were assessed separately.
issues.related: [PR #5334](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5334): compile await inside an async comprehension

issues.title: AST round trip for a starred subscript
issues.result: The original starred subscript unparses to valid syntax and reparses; extended combinations preserve AST structure.
issues.expected: Unparsing A[1:2, *l] must yield a valid subscript expression.
issues.limits: The claim covers the reported syntax and selected round-trip variants.
issues.related: [PR #5121](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5121): valid subscript-tuple unparsing

issues.title: Email Subject with an unknown encoding
issues.result: The original X-encoded Subject is returned without KeyError. Unknown encodings and related malformed-header controls were also checked.
issues.expected: Retrieving the reported Subject must recover from the unknown encoded-word encoding.
issues.limits: Successful recovery is not a guarantee for every malformed email header.
issues.related: [PR #5663](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5663): unknown encoded-word recovery

issues.title: Bool numeric format codes
issues.result: False and True match CPython for the original codes, the comment's n/d codes and width/precision controls: 34 recorded results.
issues.expected: Explicit numeric format codes must format bool through its numeric value.
issues.limits: Locale was C for this issue. The broader locale defects in #4613 and #5181 are separate.
issues.related: [PR #5012](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/5012): update the parser/format dependency · [Parser PR #91](https://github.com/RustPython/Parser/pull/91)

issues.title: Locale formatting with LC_ALL unset
issues.result: With LC_ALL absent and LANG/LC_NUMERIC=en_US.UTF-8, the unmodified original test_locale and two int/float locale tests pass, with no skip or expectedFailure.
issues.expected: The original test must use locale grouping after setlocale(LC_ALL, "") even when LC_ALL is absent from the environment.
issues.limits: The active comma grouping was verified; a C-locale skip is not counted. This narrower bare-n symptom is distinct from the outstanding width/padding issues.
issues.related: [PR #7350](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7350): use locale grouping, separator and decimal-point data

issues.title: Builtin buffer methods
issues.result: Seven builtin/subclass types expose the expected buffer behavior. Writable flags, release, blocked resize during export and successful resize after release agree with CPython.
issues.expected: Builtin buffer providers must expose the Python-facing PEP 688 methods where appropriate.
issues.limits: __release_buffer__ is optional for types that do not need it. Full C ABI coverage and all lifetime/concurrency combinations were not tested.
issues.related: [PR #8523](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8523): PEP 688 methods and managed buffer exports

issues.title: Locale-aware n formatting
issues.result: Bare n and the original locale test pass, but en_US format(123456789, "015n") gives 0000123,456,789 instead of CPython's 000,123,456,789.
issues.expected: Locale grouping must also remain correct when n formatting is combined with zero padding.
issues.limits: The locale exists and grouping is active. Both outputs have length 15; the defect is grouping, not missing locale setup.
issues.related: [PR #7350](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7350): use locale grouping, separator and decimal-point data

issues.title: Invalid escape warning in a bytes literal
issues.result: The bytes value is preserved and compilation emits the required SyntaxWarning for the invalid escape. Warning presence and warning-as-error behavior were checked.
issues.expected: Compilation of the original bytes literal must report the invalid escape while preserving its value.
issues.limits: Exit 0 alone is not the oracle; warning output is required.
issues.related: [PR #7164](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7164): warn about invalid string and bytes escapes

issues.title: Blockers for colored tracebacks
issues.result: All four listed blockers execute successfully. Colored traceback APIs and four actual uncaught exception paths match CPython, including builtin and missing-stdlib suggestions.
issues.expected: Class-pattern code generation, frame.f_builtins, sys.stdlib_module_names and except* code generation must support traceback rendering.
issues.limits: The eight uncaught-exception processes correctly exit 1. The check does not certify every traceback edge case or terminal.
issues.related: [PR #6110](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6110): class-pattern code generation; [PR #6568](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6568): provide both frame.f_builtins and sys.stdlib_module_names; [PR #6530](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6530): except* code generation and exception-group handling

issues.title: Py_GIL_DISABLED configuration value
issues.result: sysconfig.get_config_var("Py_GIL_DISABLED") is defined as 1 in the verified POSIX RustPython build.
issues.expected: The tested RustPython build must expose its build-time Py_GIL_DISABLED setting instead of None.
issues.limits: CPython can legitimately return a different value. This is not proof of full free-threading or C-extension compatibility.
issues.related: [PR #6428](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/6428): expose the build-time Py_GIL_DISABLED value

issues.title: XZ support and the forced lzma skip
issues.result: The forced skip is gone and basic XZ operations pass. However, identical CPython-generated XZ input returns 0 bytes from the first decompress(max_length=100) call in RustPython, versus 100 bytes in CPython.
issues.expected: The original request conditions removal of the forced skip on working XZ support.
issues.limits: The corresponding existing test is an expectedFailure, not a pass. Its marker was retained. The remaining concrete streaming defect prevents closure.
issues.related: [PR #7896](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7896): remove the unconditional lzma skip override; [PR #7756](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/7756): XZ support

issues.title: Ellipsis type name
issues.result: The name and repr are `ellipsis` and `<class 'ellipsis'>`; the types alias, JSON error note and existing JSON regression tests also pass.
issues.expected: The Ellipsis singleton type must use the CPython-visible name ellipsis.
issues.limits: No first-fixing revision was determined.
issues.related: [PR #8580](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8580): correct the Ellipsis type name

issues.title: Classmethod and staticmethod annotations
issues.result: Both wrappers support the two annotation attributes, cache values in the wrapper, and isolate writes/deletes from the wrapped function. The original unresolved-name input and regression test pass.
issues.expected: PEP 749 annotation attributes on classmethod/staticmethod must be writable, cached and independent of the original callable.
issues.limits: CPython 3.14.6 is the reference; this is not compared to older eager-annotation semantics.
issues.related: [PR #8701](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPython/pull/8701): cache and assign annotation attributes on the wrapper
